block.title: Surface aftermath: unbroken swallows and one fading ring of teal in the deep
block.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, limited saturated palette, widescreen arcade composition, subtle CRT scanline glow; ending scene painted at hi-resolution, minimal and enormous, ultra-detailed large-format art with pixel-texture accents. Almost nothing, said at maximum scale: a totally flat, empty post-storm ocean under a low slate-and-cream cloud ceiling at grey dawn, the horizon dead straight and splitting the frame exactly in two, sea-line rimmed in pale silver. On the water's face there is no ship above it — until you look down. Beneath the surface, the water itself is holding the shape of what just passed: a faint, vast, slow-fading silhouette of an ark diving at a shallow angle into the depths, suggested only by a broad smudge of deeper blue, a scattering of silver bubbles trailing off its tail end toward nothing, and along the length of its descending back a single diminishing line of cold teal porthole-glow — a string of lamps going out one by one from front to back as the deep claims the last of them. The highest, last-glowing lamp is still a small hard star under the water, the deepest is already invisible. The upper half of the frame, the whole empty world of air and cloud, does not react to this at all. Nothing else exists in the image: no land, no birds, no foreground fighter. The painting is the difference between a surface that looks peaceful and a depth that knows. Palette of slate blue, pearl grey, dawn cream, and one thinning thread of teal light under the water, lifted deep-navy shadows, never pure black. No text, no letters, no UI.

block.notes: Underwater glow thread ~#6ad8e0→#16485a; cloud cream ~#f0e0c8 over slate. The hardest spec is the invisibility gradient — the ark must be *suggested* under the surface, never drawn. If either model paints the silhouette at full opacity, swap to "readable only as displaced darkness and bubbles." Dead-straight, dead-center horizon is the frame's spine; regenerate tilted ones. A very strong poster candidate as-is.
